scope: Complete local LumaQuote workflow including staff API, direct Supabase paths, worker, media, model tools, integrations and browser

assessments.reason: The reviewed surface inventory (backend reference) maps the staff API, signed gateway, direct Supabase paths and outbound adapters, and the local trust transitions are tested. Open: the live Meta, Google and OpenAI boundaries and the tunnel are unverified, and no written threat model covers them.

Missing, malformed, wrong-scheme and forged bearer tokens are refused and an Auth outage fails closed with 503 (tested), and revoked membership blocks a live token. Expired, wrong-issuer and wrong-audience tokens still need Supabase-signed fixtures.
Staff and worker interfaces need full allowed/forbidden role tests, including future admin integration operations.
Scoped reads are tested; all update/export/resume/media objects still need cross-tenant negative coverage.
Strict request schemas reject undeclared fields; verify every future mutation/tool/Google import path before coverage.
Restricted local API RLS is exercised; complete direct REST/RPC/Storage, all writer operations, and elevated-function checks remain.
Membership revocation blocks existing tokens in tests; role downgrade, session rotation, and stream/file revocation require more evidence.

Ignored environment files and backend-only secrets exist, and a scanner (npm run check:secrets, last step of the gates) found no populated secret value, in plain, URL-encoded or base64 form, in 970 tracked, built, log and evidence files. Still open: git history and other branches, secrets not yet populated (WhatsApp), trace canaries at a live export, and key rotation.

The staff API allows only the exact local Vite origins with a fixed method and header allowlist and no credentials; foreign, lookalike, null, other-port and https origins receive no grant on preflight or simple requests, and disallowed methods/headers fail preflight. Mutating the allowlist to '*' failed the test. Limits: server headers only (no browser-run enforcement) and local origins; a deployed origin needs its own review.

Staff requests attach bearer tokens explicitly; Auth state is in sessionStorage, the API has no credential-cookie fallback, and CORS does not enable credential cookies. Reassess if cookie-authenticated routes are introduced.
React text rendering is used; hostile snippets/links/filenames and production header policy remain to verify.
Queries are parameterized and processor commands fixed; hostile values through all provider/tool/document/Sheet paths remain to exercise.

Inbound WhatsApp media is fetched only after the metadata URL is HTTPS on a Meta host (lookalike, plain-HTTP and foreign hosts refused before the bearer token is attached), redirects are refused, type and size are bounded and the body is streamed with a cap; the Graph host and endpoints are fixed. Verified with a mock transport and unit cases, and mutation (removing the host check) failed the matching tests. Limits: real Meta media URLs and redirects, and the OpenAI/LangSmith SDK destinations (fixed by their clients/config) were not exercised against hostile endpoints.
Actual constrained-container PDF/image/audio tests pass; API byte admission, decoder resource attacks, and complete output-bound tests remain.

Every per-user, per-conversation and queue limit has an integration test (reads 120, catalog search 30, mutations 30, replies 10, decisions 10, uploads 6, customer messages 6 per conversation, queue 100) and denied attempts keep counting. Open gap: a request that fails after the check (409, 404) rolls its increment back, so failed requests are never limited (strict xfail); the fixed window can admit twice the limit across a minute boundary; proxy identity is unverified. Awaiting the user's decision on committing the counter independently.

Shared estimated reservations, child-operation run caps and lost-response retention have actual local DB tests; simultaneous last-budget callers and the full release boundary still need verification. See semantic-progress.json and recovery tests; no actual-billing claim.

The 100-job queue cap returns a recoverable 503 (tested) and the worker caps running jobs at two with conversation serialization and leases. Open: the queue cap is global, so one tenant can fill it for all; worker capacity under multi-process contention and overload responsiveness are not tested.

Provider deadlines exist and a database or Storage outage returns a safe retryable 503 with recovery (tested); Drive export and Graph sends retry up to five attempts. Open: no jitter or circuit breaker, no overall request deadline across provider chains, and provider 429 handling is exercised only against stand-ins.
Scoped mutation replay is tested; concurrent replay, denied reauthorization, and uncertain live external outcomes remain.
Manual approval and outbox share a real transaction; crash-point and concurrent transaction behavior remain.
Schema constraints are installed; invalid direct writes and full referential-domain invariant tests remain.

Two independent RLS connections editing one version yield one revision and one explicit conflict; a dispatcher waiting on human ownership cannot deadlock takeover; a queued job cannot create a revision or clarification after staff review, approval or rejection; the browser flow preserves a stale edit and its precondition (all in the 2026-11-03 full run). Limits: two simultaneous approvals of one revision and a source change at finalization are not raced directly; connections, not processes across machines.

Bounded expired-job reconciliation fences old workers, retains unknown usage and exposes pending media interruption; real two-connection locking tests pass. Heartbeats, reconciliation UI and external unknown-send recovery remain unfinished.

Meta webhook handshake, raw-byte signature, bounds, durable deduplicated ingress and monotonic receipt ordering are implemented and tested with a mock transport, and the Google export protocol is replay-protected; Meta and Google acceptance of real payloads, tunnel reachability and live receipts remain unverified.

Model extraction cannot approve, send or confirm fields; transcripts and label readings are data that create no quote, approval, price change or reply echo (19 hostile-content cases), a latest-written-order gate has 40 policy cases and persisted-graph denial/resume checks, malicious catalog prose cannot become commercial instructions, and the development set includes an injection family (59/60, zero unauthorized sends, synthetic assets). Limits: no holdout run, no human speech or camera photos, and model behavior is sampled, not proven.

Similarity cannot replace explicit model codes or violate specs and never returns another tenant's records; a changed source, record, page or active status invalidates cached candidates; an edit during provider work aborts publication; suggestions carry current source versions and pages and need a written selection (semantic and retrieval tests in the 2026-11-03 full run). Limits: paid embedding quality and frozen-holdout Recall@5 are unmeasured; ACL changes beyond retiring a source are not modeled.

Exact-revision approval is idempotent on replay and rejects stale revisions; a persisted review resumes in a new worker without redrafting, a pause resumes once on a written restatement, an extra queued job cannot resume clarification or duplicate a question, and revoked staff access after queueing blocks delivery (graph-restart, manual-workflow and staff-reply tests). Limits: external callbacks from live Meta and Google are not exercised; participation by real customers is simulated.

Trace payloads are masked inside the LangSmith client (inputs, outputs, metadata, error strings and keys): nested tool, subgraph, exception, job-payload and metadata canaries never reach the exporter, worker logs and durable rows keep only safe codes on provider failure, and a live trace read back from LangSmith showed content with the planted secret and phone masked. A nested probe found that run error strings escaped masking until anonymizer=mask was added. Limits: a phone number spelled in words and customer names are not masked by design; the live canary predates the error-string fix and did not exercise a failing node; LangSmith retention is outside this app.
Consequential local audit events exist; alert conditions, audit mutation resistance, and full decision-to-result correlation remain.
Local services bind to loopback; external TLS/tunnel and integration credential handling/rotation still need live verification.

No-store, nosniff, no-referrer and frame denial are tested on every response of both processes and the authorized PDF is no-store. Pagination limits, signed document capabilities and proxy/cache behavior in a deployed setting remain.
Loopback setup and disabled-live defaults exist; unsafe/missing configuration and ingress surface isolation need complete tests.
Lockfiles and runtime npm audit are checked. clasp development-only optional MCP zod advisory is triaged in phase-1 evidence; Python audit and complete artifact review remain.

All 15 migrations apply in order to a disposable database and the resulting luma schema (columns, constraints, indexes, policies, grants, functions, triggers, RLS flags) equals the live local schema, with a negative check; a pending job and conversation survive the later five files; anon and authenticated hold no grants and the Storage bucket is private. Limits: migrations are forward-only (no rollback files; restore from backup is the rollback), pending approvals and quotes across an upgrade and production-size data are untested, and the local database was bootstrapped outside the Supabase CLI ledger.

scripts/backup_restore_drill.py dumps the luma and public (checkpoint) schemas, restores into a scratch database, compares per-company row counts, content hashes and checkpoint counts, round-trips the Storage objects and removes every artifact; a populated isolated tenant restored identically in about 0.3 s. Limits: logical dump only (no volume snapshot or point-in-time recovery), Supabase Auth stubbed with user ids, local only, not scheduled, and no seven-day backup retention exists because the drill keeps no backup.

scripts/retention.py deletes runtime media after seven days and idle conversations, checkpoints, objects, audit and inbox rows after 90 days (tested). Still open: nothing schedules it, Drive copies and provider-side copies are not deleted, backups are not aged, and customer phone numbers need an explicit policy review.
Decimal, stock/pack, discount, expiry checks and canonical PDF tests pass; broader currency/time/effective-source boundary regressions remain.

Apps Script-only Google integration is approved; concurrent GAS evidence records its own live limits. Synthetic Responses/voice/photo and embedding plumbing canaries passed; live full-graph semantic quality, Meta integration and complete provider contracts remain pending.

Targeted deny, race, restart and recovery tests run through the real API, Auth and PostgreSQL: per-endpoint limits and queue capacity, two-connection edit and takeover races, lease expiry with fencing, crash/restart resume, database and Storage outages, clean install and upgrade, populated backup/restore, forged and replayed webhooks, and stand-in versus live labeling in every evidence file. Limits: concurrency is two connections on one machine, not multi-process or multi-host; no live provider failure injection; the failed-request rate-limit gap is a strict xfail.

Fourteen views (six pages and a populated conversation, desktop and portrait) pass axe, overflow, landmark, naming and WCAG 2.2 24 px target-size checks after fixes; the 3D scene is lazy, falls back under reduced motion and has an accessible name; stale-edit and honest-state flows are browser-tested and the overview text was scanned for credential, email and phone patterns. Open: reconnect behavior, approved/failed-media/error page states in the axe run, and any screen-reader or real-device review.
The approved v1 has no anonymous public playground or hosting. The local test-customer route requires authenticated staff and cannot send real customer messages.

The staff API's 18 operations and the signed gateway's 6 are pinned by a test (all staff operations need a bearer credential except liveness; the gateway has no staff route and no documentation endpoints), and browser-facing Supabase roles hold no grants with a private Storage bucket; the inventory table in the backend reference lists the outbound adapters. Limits: the staff API serves /docs and /openapi.json unauthenticated (acceptable only while local); the adapter list is reviewed by reading, not enforced by a test.
